answer: The stationmaster sets every clock by the midday time signal, and the setting is written in the station log beside the date. A karst clock set by guess fails the log: the hands must match the time signal at the voyage of the setting, and a clock set wrong runs minutes out by dusk. Faking a month of clock settings means bribing the stationmaster, forging thirty entries and paying 6,500, while the copper page in the log is checked at every timetable change, so a station whose clocks were never set runs its trains late.
